971	### Step 1a — Noise Floor Rule — REQUIRED
972	
973	Every evaluation metric has a measurement noise floor — repeated runs of the
974	same config produce slightly different scores. A single "near-miss" DISCARD
975	whose delta is inside that noise band is **indistinguishable from having
976	changed nothing**. It is NOT a gradient, NOT a signal, and does NOT justify a
977	follow-up fine-bracket experiment.
978	
979	**You MUST read the current empirical noise floor from
980	`knowledge/noise_floor.md` (team-local) or the main-workspace canonical
981	noise file before applying this rule.** Do NOT use hardcoded thresholds.
982	If the file does not exist, the noise floor is unknown and you must not
983	close any axis on single-sample evidence; instead, post a `[SUGGESTION]`
984	requesting a seed-variance infrastructure probe and treat all recent
985	near-miss DISCARDs as "axis remains open, not enough data." Once the
986	file exists, the meaningful quantities for this rule are the composite
987	1σ (combining cross-seed and same-seed components, if known) and the 2σ
988	and 4σ multiples of it — use those as the near-miss band, not any
989	historical fixed number.
990	
991	Rules when auditing recent DISCARDs against that band:
992	
993	- **Delta inside the noise band, only 1 data point on the axis:**
994	  - Do NOT add the axis to `dead_ends.md` — it is still open
995	  - Do NOT propose a fine-bracket follow-up from this single point
996	  - Require **at least 2 data points** on the axis before either action
997	- **Delta clearly outside the noise band (positive or negative):** treat as
998	  real signal and proceed normally
999	- **2+ DISCARDs inside the noise band pointing opposite directions:** the
1000	  axis is flat in this neighborhood — close it in `dead_ends.md` as "flat,
1001	  no gradient"
1002	
1003	**Far / opposite probe rule (extends the above):** when a single near-miss
1004	is your ONLY signal on an axis, the next proposal on that axis must be
1005	either (a) a **far probe** — a value much further from the current optimum
1006	than the near-miss — or (b) an **opposite-direction probe** — a value on
1007	the other side of the current optimum. Do NOT propose a fine-bracket
1008	half-way between the current optimum and the near-miss. Fine-brackets are
1009	only legitimate after a 2-point monotone trend has already been
1010	established. This rule prevents near-miss avalanches where each
1011	fine-bracket re-confirms noise and closes nothing.
1012	
1013	**Bracketed-minimum pre-refinement check:** before approving ANY fine-bracket
1014	refinement around a bracketed minimum, compute `best_observed_delta - 0`
1015	and compare it to the noise floor. **If the best bracketed delta is
1016	already above the noise band, refining the bracket cannot reach a KEEP** —
1017	the axis is arithmetically exhausted even though the shape looks
1018	"interesting". Close the axis in `dead_ends.md` instead of spending another
1019	slot on a refinement that can at best re-confirm the shallow trough.
1020	A 3-point bracket whose minimum is already above noise-band is a closed
1021	axis, not a candidate for a 4th point.
1022	
1023	**Why this matters:** without a noise-floor check, near-misses trigger
1024	fine-bracket follow-ups that mostly re-confirm noise, consuming GPU budget
1025	while adding no information. Enforce the rule even when a result "feels
1026	close" to a KEEP.
